### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5f3c03820e08fc1a3fe418053befff76d33f321b` — the merge of head `7f787656bc41c7e639c4295c85cc4d7ce2b31d9a` into base `0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5f3c03820e08fc1a3fe418053befff76d33f321b && git checkout 5f3c03820e08fc1a3fe418053befff76d33f321b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769 7f787656bc41c7e639c4295c85cc4d7ce2b31d9a && git checkout -B drift-repro 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769 && git merge --no-ff 7f787656bc41c7e639c4295c85cc4d7ce2b31d9a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: ACCEPT** · PR #34520 · card #34392 · first review · read 2026-11-17T00:21Z

Head-sha: `7f787656bc41c7e639c4295c85cc4d7ce2b31d9a` (the head named in final-head comment 6933580665)

Read from GitHub at this head (`get_files`, diff, check-runs), not from the report.

**Checklist**
- Shape: draft, base `main`. The body opens with the attribution lines, then `Fixes #34392`, and the whole card is delivered. The other numbers in the body (#33985, #34062, #14788, #15387) have no closing verb next to them.
- Scope: 7 files, all on the claim's file surface (claim 6930996341: the console's language reads, `current-user-endpoints.ts` "only if the server half needs it", root changeset). The server half is needed, and the body's premise section shows why. No `content/docs/releases/`.
- Changeset: root, patch for `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` and `@object-ui/console`. I checked each sentence against the diff:
  - The resolution order in the changeset matches `locale: stored ?? requested ?? organization ?? deployment.locale`, with `requestedServedLocale` (top tag through `resolveLocaleAmong` over `i18n.getLocales()`, else the declared default) and `organizationDefaultLocale` (`resolveOrganizationLocale` from `@objectstack/core`).
  - "answered in the app's own spelling (`en-US` → `en`, `ja` → `ja-JP`)" holds, and the changeset states this value change in plain view.
  - "A host with no `i18n` service … the request's language answers as before" holds: `servedLocales` gives `undefined` there and the raw tag passes.
  - "a host with no `settings` service keeps the cascade's answer" holds through the early `undefined` return.
  - "The Console now states a language only when the app lists the browser's language" holds: `pickPreferredLocale` lost its `appDefault` fallback, and that parameter has no other caller at this head.
  - "No response key or discovery key is added" holds: the `CurrentUserLocalization` shape is untouched.
- Tests: six new server cases in `current-user-endpoints-localization.test.ts`, with a CONTROL for a supported browser language and cases for a stored `sys_user.locale`, no org setting, a failed org read and no `i18n` service. On the console side, three existing pins are rewritten on purpose (see Deviations below), and CONTROLs cover the no-org fallback and a supported language beating the org setting.
- Gates: 53 check-runs on this head, all `completed`: 43 `success`, 10 `skipped`, 0 failed. Lint & Repo Gates `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`, Test Core `success`, Test UI `success`, Type Check UI `success`.

**Narrowing question (the area asked for a ruling): not narrowing, `Clause-②: no` stands, L2 not owed.**
- The criterion (`execution-duties.md`): `Clause-②` is about widening the accepted set or enlarging the public surface; narrowing is narrowing the published accepted set.
- Read on this diff: every `Accept-Language` value is still accepted with the same 200 and the same response keys. Nothing is refused, no key is added, and no type changes. What changes is which rung answers `locale` for a tag the app does not list, plus the app-spelling normalization. That is an output-value change inside the ladder the maintainer ruled (6915665005), not a change to the accepted set.
- The published summary of the ladder (`packages/spec/src/api/auth.zod.ts:58-60` docblock and `:76-77` tombstone text: "sys_user.locale → the request's Accept-Language → the deployment default") still holds at rung granularity. The rung order is unchanged, and conditions are added inside rungs 2 and 3, so this round does not make that published text false. No spec edit is owed.

**Spot checks (mine)**
1. The organization read is skipped when rung 2 already answers (`requested ? undefined : …`), and otherwise runs beside the other two reads in the same `Promise.all`. So the endpoint adds no round trip on the first-visit race the comment names.
2. A throwing settings read is caught, `warn`ed and falls to the cascade, as the "never an error" test pins. A throwing `i18n` probe is caught in `servedLocales` and falls back to the raw tag. Neither path can turn the endpoint into a 500.
3. For a console user with an unsupported browser language and no org setting, the answer stays the app's declared default (now via the server's rung 3 instead of the console stating it), which is the old behaviour. The no-org CONTROL pins it.

**Deviations accepted**
- Three existing console pins are rewritten, not left as they were. They encoded "an unsupported browser language states the app default", which this card retires by the same ruling's order. They were replaced, not deleted, and the replacements assert the new rung.
- The quick-read's risk line names the unsupported-language change. The `en-US` → `en` normalization of a supported language is the other visible value change for a third-party client; the changeset states it, so a reader of the release notes sees it.

**L2 owed: no.** None of the four contract faces is touched: `Clause-②: no`, no narrowing (above), no `packages/spec/src/**` path, no governed rule text.

**Landing tier**: `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34520` reports NOT governed, +369/−87 = 456 lines ≤ 3000. Ordinary queue landing by the area at this head.
